title: Prospective randomised study of different surgical techniques to prevent postoperative lymphoceles after robot-assisted laparoscopic radical prostatectomy and their impact on peri- and postoperative morbidity and quality of life
summary:
The patient was diagnosed with prostate cancer and, after receiving information from the treating physicians, decided to undergo surgical removal of the prostate. Given the patient's risk profile, it was discussed with him that lymph nodes adjacent to the prostate that were at risk would also be removed during the operation. One of the most common side effects of this procedure is the accumulation of lymph fluid (lymphoceles). This accumulation and encapsulation of lymph fluid is caused by the severing of the lymph vessels. In some cases, lymphoceles can cause pressure discomfort, venous drainage disorders from the lower parts of the body and infections. This can significantly increase the occurrence of diseases, complications or adverse events throughout the postoperative course. According to current studies, risk factors for developing a lymphocele appear to be an elevated body mass index (BMI), the number of lymph nodes removed and a prolonged hospital stay. Urologists who perform surgery strive to avoid this side effect as much as possible.
The number of new cases of prostate cancer in Germany in 2020 was 65,820 patients. Serious lymphoceles occur in up to 11.2% of cases involving open surgery. With robot-assisted procedures, such as the one planned for you, the rate is lower at 7.9%. In the study presented here, we will only perform robot-assisted operations. Within robot-assisted surgical techniques, there are different ways to minimise the risk of lymphocele development in the postoperative course. At present, there is no uniform recommendation as to which method is most suitable for reducing the risk of lymphocele or symptomatic lymphocele. 
In summary, we want to investigate in this study whether there is a ‘best surgical approach’ to minimise the occurrence of lymphoceles after surgery. To this end, we are using combinations of different surgical methods that have already been proven to be effective and comparing which combinations are most effective in reducing lymphoceles.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Patients with prostate cancer
2. Robot-assisted radical prostatectomy (RALP) possible
3. Simultaneous lymphadenectomy
4. Capable of giving consent, willing to give consent
Exclusion criteria:
1. Multimodal therapeutic concept
2. No consent
3. Individual decision by the patient and/or surgeon not to perform/have lymphadenectomy performed as part of RALP
4. Contraindication to LAD
